description: JSON Schema for swiftcode.json (manifestVersion 1). This schema is the formalization of Docs/Intro-to-SDK.md §7 and the fixed Phase 1 decisions in SwiftCode/SDK/Documentation/SDK-Architecture.md (capability IDs ADR §7, error codes ADR §8). Forward compatibility is handled by explicit new schema versions (manifestVersion 2, new file), NOT by silent extra fields: additionalProperties is false at the top level and on capability/command objects. Constraints that cannot be expressed in draft 2020-12 (duplicate capability/command ids, entrypoint file existence, package-level checks from spec §7.2) are enforced by the strict manifest/package validator (Phase 1 work item P1b), not by this schema.

$schema.description: Pointer to the schema this manifest was authored against. In a packaged extension this MUST point to the schema file shipped with the SDK inside the extension package (e.g. "./schemas/swiftcode-extension-v1.schema.json") or a verified official URL. Dead URLs are rejected at install time per spec §7.1.

assist.description: Assist-related declaration. DESCRIPTIVE METADATA ONLY in this release: a manifest "assist": {"requested": true} does NOT grant Assist access. Assist is unavailable to extensions, period (ADR §9): any assist.invoke request -> typed ASSIST_DENIED + audit event. The future Assist authorization flow is not implemented and no dormant bypass is added.

requested.description: Whether the extension declares interest in Assist capabilities. False for the first extension.

capabilities.description: Capability grant requests. A valid manifest is a request, not an authorization token: each id still requires an explicit user grant via the CapabilityBroker, and unknown ids are rejected with UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY (never silently reinterpreted). Duplicate ids are rejected by the host validator; this schema cannot express per-property uniqueness inside arrays.

id.description: Capability IDs from the canonical SwiftCode SDK capability registry (SDKCapability.swift / ScopesIDLists.ts). No other ids may appear.

reason.description: Non-empty, plain-language justification shown to the user in the grant approval UI.

contributes.description: UI contributions. In this release only the command model is supported (no arbitrary native UI injection). Today's CommandPaletteView.CommandAction enum is closed, so command contributions need a new open registry on the host side.

commands.description: Contributed commands. Command ids must be unique within the array; uniqueness is enforced by the host validator (not expressible per-property in this draft).

id.description: Machine identifier for the command, lowercase alphanumeric plus hyphens.

title.description: Human-readable command title shown in the UI.

id.description: Reverse-DNS extension identifier, e.g. "com.example.repository-build-extension". Used as the install-directory name and the identity bound to the runtime session; extension-supplied identity is never trusted beyond this validated value.

manifestVersion.description: Manifest schema generation. This file defines generation 1. Unsupported generations are rejected with MANIFEST_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION.

entrypoint.description: Path of the entrypoint file RELATIVE to the package root. Must not be absolute and must not contain ".." segments; escaping the package root is rejected with PATH_TRAVERSAL. Existence inside the validated package is checked at install time (schema cannot check the filesystem).

language.description: Only TypeScript extensions are supported in this release (Python deferred per ADR §12).

minimumSwiftCodeVersion.description: Minimum host SwiftCode version this extension requires (semver).

name.description: The SDK package name this extension is built against.

protocolVersion.description: Host/runtime IPC contract version. Mismatches are rejected with IPC_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH.

versionRange.description: npm-style semver range for the SDK version, e.g. "^1.0.0". Incompatible ranges are rejected with INCOMPATIBLE_SDK_VERSION. This schema checks the character set only; real range satisfaction is evaluated by the host validator.

type.description: Package kind. "extension" contributes commands and UI to the host; "app" is a standalone package shipped in the identical .swiftcode-extension format (same archive layout, digest, and install directory) and distinguished by this field at runtime.

version.description: Full semver 2.0.0 of the extension package.

title: SwiftCode Extension Manifest
